description: Figure 8(d) illustrates the post-edit knowledge probing accuracy (ACC %) on the Qwen2.5 large language model as a function of the co-occurrence number, comparing five different editing methods. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 60% to 85%, with tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, and 85. Six distinct lines represent the methods: “Base” (black, solid line with circle markers), “FT” (blue, solid line with triangle markers), “IKE” (red, solid line with triangle markers), “MEND” (brown, solid line with diamond markers), “MEMIT” (purple, solid line with diamond markers), and “ROME” (green, solid line with square markers). All methods show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number grows. The “Base” model starts at approximately 63% and rises to about 70.5%. “FT” begins near 65.5% and reaches ~73%. “IKE” starts around 67% and ends at ~75%. “MEND” begins at ~70.5% and climbs to ~80.5%. “MEMIT” starts at ~70% and reaches ~77%. “ROME” consistently outperforms all others, starting at ~74% and increasing to ~83.5% at the highest co-occurrence number.
